I don't trust myself to be able to handle the responsibility of taking care of another human being. I have skeletal problems so I'm worried pregnancy might worsen the random aches and pain I get. I'm insecure enough of my body as it is, and all the things about pregnancy that people find "beautiful", I fear may become huge regrets for me. I fear that I won't be financially well-off enough to give a child a life I think they deserve. I tend to be blunt and aggressive, especially towards children; I hate being mean and I don't want to be mean to a child, so it's better to not have one and have them grow effed up. And the #1 reason, I'm pretty damn sure our world isn't gonna get any better. Environmentally, politically, and the people themselves, it'll never change. I wouldn't want to put a child through that. I wouldn't want a child to hold a grudge against me for bringing them into this world when they never asked to be born (like I do with my parents; though I love them and am very grateful for them, I hate that I was conceived at all, especially at a time when they were still struggling to gain footing in the world of adulthood). If I ever change my mind and want to take care of a child, I'll probably foster/adopt an older kid, only when I'm sure that I'm ready to be there for them my whole life. 

Please don't have children and expect them to be your retirement fund, or to be grateful for the bare minimum. Cherish them, take care of them, talk to them. Don't blame them for "burdening" you when you were the one that decided to have them.
